question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
The certified Act gives six months: an officer or employee who wishes to opt out may do so "within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute" [Act 20/2025 §33(2)(b)].

- This is an Act (Act No. 20 of 2025, certified 2025-10-07), not a bill — the "proposed" law has been passed [Act 20/2025 §33].
- Employees who decline are paid compensation under a voluntary retirement scheme approved by the Minister and the Minister of Finance [Act 20/2025 §33(2)(c)].

Caveats: The evidence contains only this passage, and a note on it says the decision period may be truncated or incomplete; the six-month figure above is what the quoted sub-paragraph (b) states.

question: Under the proposed Inland Revenue amendment, from which assessment date are deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act excluded from subsection (2)?
answer:
Under the certified Inland Revenue (Amendment) Act, No. 11 of 2026, the exclusion applies to deductions under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act for **any year of assessment prior to 1 April 2018** [Act 11/2026 §34].

- The new section 202(2A)(a) says subsection (2) “shall not apply” to such deductions, even if an un-deducted balance remains as at 1 April 2018 [Act 11/2026 §34].

Caveat: this is an amending Act; the full amended text of the principal Act is not in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law, how long does a licence issued or renewed remain in effect?
answer:
Under the Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority Act, No. 9 of 2026 (certified 2026-03-20), a licence issued under section 23 or renewed under section 24 is "valid for a period of one year" and must "specify the date of expiry"; it is non-transferable [Act 9/2026 §25]. This is an Act, not a bill.

- Renewal applications must be made "not less than sixty days prior to the date of the expiry of the licence" [Act 9/2026 §24(1)(a)].
- Late applications may be accepted up to thirty days before expiry, subject to an administrative charge not exceeding rupees two million [Act 9/2026 §24(2)].

Caveats: The 2016 Micro Finance Bill proposed a different rule (valid until 31 December following grant) [006/2016 §5], but that is a proposal, not law.

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer:
Under section 6(1) of the Licensing of Container Depot Operators Act, No. 3 of 2026, the renewal application must be submitted "not less than thirty days prior to the date of expiration of the licence previously issued" [Act 3/2026 §6].

- It must be in the prescribed Form, accompanied by the prescribed renewal fee [Act 3/2026 §6].
- The Director-General must renew if the licence terms were not violated, the Act/regulations not contravened, and there is no adverse public impact [Act 3/2026 §6].

Caveats: This is the certified Act (certified 2026-02-17), not a bill; the text sets a minimum of thirty days and no longer period.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, what is the new maximum duration a freezing order may be in effect?
answer:
Under the certified Prevention of Money Laundering (Amendment) Act, No. 16 of 2026 (2026-08-04), the maximum in section 8(2)(b) of the principal Act rises from "three months" to "four months" [Act 16/2026 §9].

- The same clause replaces "a period of two years" with "a period of three years" [Act 16/2026 §9] — the evidence does not show which limit this refers to.
- Separately, the initial police order period goes from "seven days" to "fourteen working days" [Act 16/2026 §8].

Caveats: This is an amending Act, not the principal Act's consolidated text; the evidence does not state whether "four months" or "three years" is the overall maximum duration, so I cannot confirm which is the true cap.

question: Under the amended Telecommunication Levy law, how often is the levy calculated on the value of telecom services received?
answer:
The bill proposes that the levy be computed **on the value of telecom services received "in respect of each month"** — i.e. monthly — but this is only a proposal, not law.

- The substitution for section 2 of the Telecommunication Levy Act, No. 21 of 2011 charges the levy "on the value of the supply of telecommunication services provided by any operator or provider, on the receipt of such telecommunication services in respect of each month" [028/2026 §2].
- The same clause is in Bill 035/2026 (Bill, 2026-05-06); the identical text appears in the Gazette text of 2026-04-23 [035/2026].
- The older proposal used the same monthly basis ("in respect of each month") [006/2015 §2]; the 2011 bill did too [011/2011 §2].

Caveats: No certified Act is held for the 2026 amendment (Acts checked to 2026-10-30), so it has not been shown to have passed; the monthly wording is proposed, not enacted in that form. The amending bill changes the principal Act, whose full text is not in the evidence.

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
Under the Bills of Exchange (Amendment) Act, No. 13 of 2025, notice of dishonour may be given "in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means" that sufficiently identify the bill and intimate dishonour [Act 13/2025 §8].

- This is an amending Act: it repeals and substitutes section 49(5) of the Bills of Exchange Ordinance (Chapter 82), so the wording quoted is the new subsection, not the Ordinance's full current text [Act 13/2025 §8].
- The electronic route requires the means to "sufficiently identify the bill, and intimate that the bill has been dishonoured by non-acceptance or non-payment" [Act 13/2025 §8].
- An earlier bill, 552/2024 (2024-08-21), was not itself law; the Act above is what became law [552/2024].

Caveats: The evidence does not set out section 49's other subsections.

question: Under the proposed Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation incorporation law, who is defined as a qualified auditor?
answer:
The Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation (Incorporation) bill defines a "qualified auditor" in its accounts-and-audit clause as either an individual or a firm holding practice certification from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or another institute established by law) [626/2025 §11(4)].

- Individual: "a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka, or any other Institute established by law" holding "a certified to practice as Accountant issued by the Council of such Institute" [626/2025 §11(4)(a)].
- Firm: a firm of accountants whose resident partners each meet that membership and certificate requirement [626/2025 §11(4)(b)].
- The audit is by such an auditor "appointed by Auditor General in terms of Article 154 of the Constitution" [626/2025 §11(3)].

Caveats: this is a bill (2025-07-23), not law — no certified Act is held, so it has not been shown to have passed. The passage's wording is slightly garbled in places ("a certified to practice"); the definition quoted is that text as published.

question: What is meant by “knowledge sharing activities” under the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture Act?
answer:
The only evidence is a bill, not an Act: the Gazette text of the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture (Incorporation) Bill defines it as "activities designed to facilitate to exchange of ideas, skills, and experiences fostering on culture of learning and collaboration" [646/2025 §18].

- It is an interpretation clause definition ("In this Act, unless the context otherwise required"), and the quoted wording appears as printed, including the phrasing "facilitate to exchange" and "fostering on culture" [646/2025 §18].
- No certified Act is held, so this definition has not been shown to have passed into law [646/2025 §18].

Caveats: The bill's short title adds "(Incorporation)"; no Act text is available to confirm the final wording.

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
The Bill (not yet shown to have passed) lets the Society "take and hold any property, movable or immovable," held for the Act's purposes and subject to rules under section 7 [047/2026 §13].

- It may obtain land or buildings by "purchase, rent, construct, renovate" and deal with or dispose of them as the Council determines [047/2026 §6(a)].
- It may hold real or personal property under a lawful trust with similar objects [047/2026 §6(f)].
- It has power to "sell, mortgage, lease, exchange, or otherwise dispose of" such property [047/2026 §13], with its administration and management governed by rules made under section 7 [047/2026 §7(1)(f)].

Caveats: This is a proposal only — no certified Act held (Acts checked to 2026-10-30); the Gazette text (041/2026) carries identical wording.

question: In the Institute of Real Estate Professionals, who chairs the Membership and Policy Advisory committees, and how are chairs selected for the remaining committees?
answer:
Under the Act now in force, the President of the Institute chairs both committees: the "Membership Committee" and the "Policy Advisory and Constitutional Committee" [Act 6/2026 §18(1)(a)–(b), (2)]. For the rest, each committee must include at least one Council member, who is its Chairperson [Act 6/2026 §18(2)]; if more than one Council member is appointed, the Council picks one as Chairperson [Act 6/2026 §18(3)].

- The Act uses "Chairperson" where the bills said "Chairman" — same office, changed wording [Act 6/2026 §18(2)].
- Chair presides at meetings; in their absence members elect a presiding Chairperson [Act 6/2026 §18(5)].

Caveats: The bill versions (637/2025, 656/2025 §18) are proposals only; the Act governs. Details of composition are left to rules [Act 6/2026 §18(4)].

question: Under the amended Colombo Port City Economic Commission law, how is the income tax treatment of workers hired by licensed businesses affected depending on whether the licence was granted before or after the new provisions take effect?
answer:
Under the certified Colombo Port City Economic Commission (Amendment) Act, No. 1 of 2026, workers of businesses licensed **before** the new section commenced get a temporary income-tax exemption; workers of businesses licensed **on or after** commencement are taxable.

- For pre-commencement licensees, resident and non-resident employees’ “employment income” is “exempt from income tax” for “a period of three years” from the month after commencement [Act 1/2026 §3].
- Non-resident employees are also “not be liable to income tax in Sri Lanka on any income earned outside Sri Lanka” [Act 1/2026 §3].
- For licences granted “on or after” commencement, employment income “shall be liable to income tax” [Act 1/2026 §3].

Caveats: This is an amending Act; it states the substituted section 35, not the full current text of the 2021 Act.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
The certified Act amends the 1972 Act’s long title by substituting “freight forwarders and non-vessel operating common carriers” for “freight forwarders, non-vessel operating common carriers, and container operators”, thereby removing the reference to container operators. [Act 4/2026 §2]

- This is in Act No. 4 of 2026 (certified 2026-02-17), not the earlier bill. [Act 4/2026 §2]
- Separately, §3 substitutes the Act’s name without “Container Operators”. [Act 4/2026 §3]

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer:
The evidence does not contain a single statement of the amendment's overall purpose; Act No. 18 of 2026 (certified 2026-08-04) amends the 2005 Act only through scattered section-by-section substitutions.

- It extends the Act to offences committed "wholly or partly outside Sri Lanka" directed at Sri Lanka, a Sri Lankan citizen, a government facility, or to compel the Government [Act 18/2026 §3].
- It replaces "funds or property" with "funds, property or other assets, material support or resources" throughout, e.g. sections 3(1), 4, 4A–4F [Act 18/2026, p.18 Schedule].
- It extends freezing orders from "seven days" to "fourteen working days" [Act 18/2026 §5].

Caveats: The central/overall modification is not stated in the evidence; only individual amendments are shown.

question: Which 2025 bill outlines the government's budget and borrowing provisions for the financial year 2026?
answer:
The Appropriation Bill of 2025 — bill 639/2025 (with identical text in 632/2025) — covers FY2026; it is now **Act 23/2025** (certified 2025-12-05), so answer from the Act.

- Act 23/2025 §2(1) estimates expenditure of "rupees four thousand four hundred thirty-four billion three hundred fifty-six million four hundred sixty-eight thousand" for 1 Jan–31 Dec 2026, met from the Consolidated Fund and from borrowing in or outside Sri Lanka [Act 23/2025 §2].
- The Act caps outstanding borrowing at "rupees three thousand seven hundred forty billion", with loan details in the Final Budget Position Report under s.51 of the Public Financial Management Act, No. 44 of 2024 [Act 23/2025 §2].
- The bill as published set that cap at "rupees three thousand eight hundred billion"; the enacted figure differs [639/2025 §2].

Caveats: The change from Rs 3,800bn to Rs 3,740bn bears directly on the borrowing limit; use the Act's figure.

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
It is the **Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation)** bill — published as a Gazette text on 2026-06-15 [043/2026 §1] and presented as Bill 055/2026 on 2026-07-27 (that version spells the name "Recourses"). It is a **bill, not law**: no certified Act is held for it, so it has not been shown to have passed [055/2026].

- Objects include developing all economic sectors and "human resource development programmes" for rural youth [043/2026 §3(1)(a)–(b)], plus micro-entrepreneurship, drug-prevention and soil conservation work [043/2026 §3(1)(f)–(i)].
- Implementation must be "without any distinction based on race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth" [043/2026 §3(2)].
- The bill sets no penalties [055/2026].

Caveats: Only pre-enactment texts are in evidence; the 2026-07-27 bill repeats the 2026-06-15 Gazette wording [043/2026 §3].

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media law, what is the maximum length of a suspension the Council can impose instead of disenrolling a member?
answer:
The maximum is **one year**: the Council may, "in lieu of disenrolling a member", "suspend him from membership for such period not exceeding one year" [054/2026 §24].

- This sits alongside the lesser options of warning or reprimanding the member [054/2026 §24].
- It applies where the Disciplinary Committee's report establishes professional misconduct [054/2026 §24], that report following an inquiry under section 23 [054/2026 §23].

Caveats: This is a bill (Establishment of the Chartered Institute of Media, 2026-07-22); no certified Act is held, so it has not been shown to have passed [054/2026 §24]. Identical text appears in bills 040/2026 and 050/2026.

question: Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, how long must someone have continuously and peacefully occupied a premises to be regarded as an “occupant”?
answer:
More than three months of "undisturbed and uninterrupted occupation," and the person must also be in "lawful occupation" of the premises [004/2026 §2]. The same threshold appears in the earlier Gazette text [634/2025 §2].

- The three months must run "prior to the eventualities specified under section 3, 4 or 5" [004/2026 §2].
- The text says "undisturbed and uninterrupted," not "peacefully" as the question puts it [004/2026 §2].

Caveats: This is a bill (2026-01-20), not shown to have passed; no certified Act is held [004/2026 §2].

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
Under the Gambling Regulatory Authority Act, No. 17 of 2025 (certified 2025-09-03), a person "over seventy years of age" is disqualified from appointment as a member of the Board — so the limit is 70 [Act 17/2025 §9(i)].

- The clause is framed as a disqualification "from being appointed as a member of the Board", not expressly from continuing to serve [Act 17/2025 §9].
- It sits alongside other disqualifications, e.g. conviction for an offence of moral turpitude punishable with imprisonment of "not less than six months" [Act 17/2025 §9(d)].

Caveats: The other passages are from the Proceeds of Crime Act, No. 5 of 2025, whose Board rule is "not more than seventy years of age" as at appointment [Act 5/2025 §100(1)(a)]; that is a different law and does not govern the Gambling Regulatory Authority's Board.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, what is the longest jail term a person can receive for arriving in or departing Sri Lanka with cash or bearer‑negotiable instruments above the minister‑set limit?
answer:
The maximum is **one year's imprisonment**, under the certified Financial Transactions Reporting (Amendment) Act, No. 17 of 2026, which substitutes a new section 27 in the principal Act [Act 17/2026 §31].

- The offence is arriving in or leaving Sri Lanka with cash or bearer negotiable instruments above the sum the Minister specifies by Gazette Order (under the Foreign Exchange Act, No. 12 of 2017), without first reporting it [Act 17/2026 §31].
- On conviction by a Magistrate: a fine "not exceeding three times of the value" of the cash/instruments, or imprisonment "of either description for a term not exceeding one year", or both [Act 17/2026 §31].
- The excess sum is forfeited to the State [Act 17/2026 §31].

Caveats: This is an amending Act, so the term comes from the substituted section 27 rather than the principal Act's text as reprinted; the earlier 2005 proposal also carried a one-year maximum but is not law [020/2005 §27].

question: Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket law, what penalty amount does a member owe if they fail to pay the subscription by the deadline?
answer:
Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket law, a member who misses the deadline owes a "late payment fee equal to twice the annual subscription" [072/2026 §30(4)].

- The subscription itself is due "on or before the thirty first day of December" of the preceding year; the doubled fee is then payable by "the thirtieth day of April of the following year" [072/2026 §30(3)–(4)].
- Non-payment by that later date means automatic forfeiture of voting rights [072/2026 §30(5)].

Caveats: This is the Gazette text of a proposal, not an Act — it has not been shown to have passed [072/2026 §30]. The same text appears in 077/2026.

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
No day is fixed: the clause only identifies *which* debts pass to the body corporate — those "existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act" — and says they "shall be paid by the body corporate", with no payment deadline. [009/2026 §12]

- This is a bill ("Gazette text", 2026-02-05; also Bill 014/2026 of 2026-02-17), not law — it has not been shown to have passed. [009/2026 §12]
- A near-identically titled 2021 bill (Indira Cancer **Trust**) has the same wording, also unenacted as far as the index shows. [095/2021 §12]

Caveats: An Act, if passed, may fix a time; the evidence holds no certified text.

question: Under the proposed Immigration Bill, what is the minimum and maximum penalty imposed on a ship's master or aircraft captain who fails to report a transit passenger or crew member that appears to have stayed in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Under the Immigration Bill (082/2026), the fine is a minimum of "one hundred thousand rupees" and a maximum of "five hundred thousand rupees" [082/2026 §90(2)].

- The offence is failing to notify an Immigration Officer that a transit passenger or crew member appears to have remained in Sri Lanka [082/2026 §90(1)].
- Liability is "jointly and severally" on the master, captain or agent, on conviction [082/2026 §90(2)].

Caveats: this is a bill, not law — no certified Act has been shown. The same wording also appears in 508/2024, 513/2024 and 071/2026 [082/2026 §90].

question: Under the proposed Convention against Doping in Sport amendment, how long does the Board Chairman serve?
answer:
Under the amending Act, the Chairman holds office "for a term of three years" and is eligible for reappointment [Act 21/2025 §11]. That is now law, not a proposal: the Convention against Doping in Sport (Amendment) Act, No. 21 of 2025 was certified on 2025-10-07 [Act 21/2025 §11].

- The three-year term appears in the substituted section 14(2): the Minister appoints one appointed member as Chairman on the majority recommendation of the ex-officio members, and that Chairman serves three years, renewable [Act 21/2025 §11].
- The same Act also amends section 17(2) so removal of an appointed member requires a majority of the Board rather than the Minister [Act 21/2025 §14].

Caveats: The question says "proposed", but this is a certified Act. The evidence contains only the amending Act, not the consolidated principal Act (No. 33 of 2013) as it now reads. The 2013 Gazette text gives a three-year term for appointed members generally [044/2013 §17], but that is a bill-stage proposal, not law.

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
Under the Rubber Control (Amendment) Act, No. 16 of 2025, "Director-General" means the Director-General of the Rubber Development Department, appointed or deemed to have been appointed under the Act [Act 16/2025 §6].

- This is an amending Act: §6 repeals the definition of "Controller" in section 52 of the principal enactment and substitutes the new definition [Act 16/2025 §6].
- It is a certified Act (2025-08-22), passed from bills 595/2025 and 620/2025 [Act 16/2025].

Caveats: The evidence does not reproduce section 52 as it now stands in Chapter 436, only the amendment.

question: In the amended Personal Data Protection Act, which bodies are regarded as a public authority?
answer:
Under the amendment, "public authority" means "a Ministry, any Department, Provincial Council, local authority, or a Ministry or Department of a Provincial Council" [Act 22/2025 §14(2)].

- The same provision excludes "a public corporation" and "a company incorporated under the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007" [Act 22/2025 §14(2)].
- This is an amending Act: it repeals and substitutes the definition in section 56 of the principal enactment (Act No. 9 of 2022), whose consolidated text is not in the evidence [Act 22/2025 §14].

Caveats: The earlier bills defined "public authority" far more broadly — including public corporations, statutory bodies and government-held companies [152/2021 §47; 167/2022 §47] — but those were proposals only; I cannot confirm how the 2022 Act originally read.

question: What criteria does the amendment set for a crop to be classified as an Export Agricultural Crop?
answer:
Under the certified Act 24/2026, a crop qualifies if it is identified as having "an export potential in addition to the local consumption", is declared by the Minister as "a notified agricultural crop" under section 2 of the principal enactment, and falls outside the excluded categories [Act 24/2026 §5].

- Excluded: "paddy, vegetables, fruits, root crops and additional food crops belonging to the category of food crops" [Act 24/2026 §5].
- Plantation crops are also excluded: "shall not include any crop identified as a plantation crop" [Act 24/2026 §5].

Caveats: This is the amending Act, which substitutes the definition in section 19 of the 1992 Act; the amended Act's consolidated text is not in the evidence. Section 2's notification procedure is referred to but not reproduced.

question: Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
Under the Chiththa bill, "qualified auditor" is defined in clause 10(4) as either an individual, or a firm whose resident partners are individuals, holding membership of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or any other institute established by law) plus a certificate to practise as an Accountant issued by that institute's Council [597/2025 §10].

- Individual: "a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka, or any other institute established by law," holding "a certiﬁcate to practice as an Accountant" from the Council [597/2025 §10(4)(a)].
- Firm: "a ﬁrm of Accountants each of the resident partners of which" meets that same membership-and-certificate test [597/2025 §10(4)(b)].
- The audit is by such an auditor "appointed by Auditor General in terms of Article 154 of the Constitution" [597/2025 §10(3)].

Caveats: This is the Gazette text of a proposal, not an Act; no certified Act for it is held, so it has not been shown to have passed [597/2025 §10].

question: Under the proposed Proceeds of Crime Bill, what types of advanced investigative methods can an investigation officer employ with a magistrate’s permission?
answer:
The Proceeds of Crime Bill became the Proceeds of Crime Act, No. 5 of 2025 (certified 2025-04-30), so answer from the Act — which calls them "special investigative techniques" (the bill said "advanced investigative techniques").

- With a Magistrate's authorisation under s.56: "controlled delivery", "digital surveillance which includes the interception and recording of digital, voice, video communication", "undercover operations including those involving the use of decoys", "laying of traps", and "forensic extraction of data, information and images" from computers, phones and other digital devices [Act 5/2025 §60].
- Also by judicial order on any person: forensic audit, digital forensic extraction, property valuation, copying/storage of data, and forensic analysis of transactions [Act 5/2025 §61].
- Interception of private communication or surveillance within private premises needs prior Magisterial authorisation, subject to a 24-hour urgency proviso [Act 5/2025 §55(2)].

Caveats: The wording differs between the bill and the Act; the Act governs.

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka law, how many council members must be present, and must the Chairperson be among them, to constitute a quorum for a council meeting?
answer:
Five members, and the Chairperson must be one of them: the quorum is "five members including the Chairperson" [054/2026 §7]. This is from a bill — the Establishment of the Chartered Institute of Media (Bill, 2026-07-22) — and has not been shown to have passed [054/2026 §7].

- The same wording appears in the June 2026 Gazette text titled Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka [040/2026 §7] (also 050/2026).
- If the Chairperson is absent, the Vice-Chairperson presides, but the quorum rule still requires the Chairperson [054/2026 §7].

Caveats: no certified Act is held, so this is a proposal only.

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
Under the National Transport Commission (Amendment) Act, No. 8 of 2025 (certified 2025-06-20), which inserts a new section 38A into Act No. 37 of 1991, fares are set by the Commission by formula and shown by operators from the Commission's published lists.

- The Commission computes transportation service fares (including omnibus) "in accordance with the formula determined by the Commission", following the national policy on fares approved by Parliament, and specifies them by Gazette Order [Act 8/2025 §19]; it must consider stakeholders' written representations in determining the formula and revise it when necessary [Act 8/2025 §5].
- The Commission publishes fare lists on its official website, and each provider must prepare its own list in accordance with those lists and have it "displayed in a conspicuous place of the transportation vehicle" [Act 8/2025 §19].
- The Commission may inspect compliance, and failure to comply "shall be guilty of an offence under section 40" [Act 8/2025 §19].

Caveats: the §19 passage cuts off mid-sentence in subsection (3) (the inspection reference to section 39(2)), so the full offence wording is not in evidence.

question: According to the proposed Mass Foundation law, what continuous legal identity will the foundation have, what ability does it have to bring or face lawsuits, how can it manage its seal, and how is it classified for regulatory oversight?
answer:
The Mass Foundation bill gives the foundation perpetual succession under the name “Mass Foundation”, and by that name it “may sue and be sued” [025/2026 §2] (identical text in 037/2026 §2). This is a proposal only — no certified Act is held, so it has not been shown to have passed.

- Seal: it has “full power and authority to have and use a common seal and to alter the same at its pleasure” [025/2026 §2].
- Seal control: it may not be affixed except before two Committee members who sign the instrument, and it is kept in the custody of a Committee-chosen office bearer [025/2026 §15].
- Oversight: it “shall be deemed to be a Voluntary Social Service Organization” under Act No. 31 of 1980, whose provisions apply [025/2026 §2].

Caveats: both clauses come from the Gazette text of 025/2026, not an Act; no enforcement provisions for the seal rules appear in the evidence.

question: Under the amendment to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Law, when a water supply and sewerage undertaking of an industrial park is transferred to the Board, which minister is treated as the ‘Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government’ for applying Part III of the Act?
answer:
Act 20/2026 §10 inserts a new section 57A into the 1974 Law; its proviso (a) says that for an industrial estate or industrial park, “the Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government” in Part III is read as the Minister assigned the subject of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka under Article 44 or 45 of the Constitution, or the Minister assigned the subject of industries under Article 44 or 45, “as the case may be” [Act 20/2026 §10].

- This is law: certified Act No. 20 of 2026 (2026-08-18), from bill 053/2026; the same wording was earlier proposed in bill 019/2026, which was not itself law [Act 20/2026 §10]; [019/2026 §10].
- It applies to Part III as extended to industrial estates, parks and community-based organizations; a different minister is named for community-based organizations [Act 20/2026 §10].

Caveats: The proviso does not say which of the two ministers prevails where both subjects are assigned; the evidence does not resolve that.

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
Under the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill [078/2026 §33], the magistrate in whose jurisdiction an approved place of detention lies must, "without giving any advance notice" to its authority, visit it "once a month", interview the suspects and look into their well-being, and call for and inspect detention registers, Detention Orders and other documents [078/2026 §33(1)].

- If torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment is observed or alleged, he "shall forthwith make an order" for production before a Judicial Medical Officer and submission of the report [078/2026 §33(4)].
- He must give the suspect and the relevant police officer a hearing before acting under section 31 [078/2026 §33(5)].
- The authority must provide "prompt and unimpeded access" [078/2026 §33(3)].

Caveats: this is a bill (Gazette/presented text), not shown to have passed; no certified Act is held [078/2026 §33].

question: Under the Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill, which civil or commercial disagreements can be taken to mediation and which types are excluded from this law?
answer:
The Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Act, No. 13 of 2026 — now certified law, from bill 616/2025 — applies to "civil and commercial disputes" mediated under a mediation agreement, by voluntary referral, or by court referral [Act 13/2026 §2(1)].

- Excluded: disputes that must go to mediation under the Mediation Boards Act, No. 72 of 1988 or the Mediation (Special Categories of Disputes) Act, No. 21 of 2003; such disputes cannot be submitted under this Act [Act 13/2026 §2(2)–(3)].
- Also barred: disputes whose settlement "requires the inclusion of terms that can be given effect to only on a decree or order of court", including those in the Schedule — though related matters may be mediated to propose settlement terms to court [Act 13/2026 §3].

Caveats: the Schedule's list of disputes is not reproduced in the evidence, so the specific categories in it cannot be stated.

question: What audit regulations govern the financial statements of Samurdhi community‑based banking societies under the Samurdhi amendment?
answer:
Under the Samurdhi (Amendment) Act, No. 15 of 2025 (certified 2025-08-22), the accounts of samurdhi community based banking societies are audited under Article 154 of the Constitution (public corporation audit provisions) and the National Audit Act, No. 19 of 2018 [Act 15/2025 §3]. This is done by inserting new section 35A after section 35 of the Samurdhi Act, No. 1 of 2013 [Act 15/2025 §3].

- A parallel new section 28A applies the same two audit regimes to samurdhi community based banks [Act 15/2025 §2].
- No new offences or penalties are stated in the Act [Act 15/2025].

Caveats: This is an amending Act, not the consolidated text of the Samurdhi Act; the full amended provisions are not in the evidence. The bill version (614/2025, 2025-06-17) became this Act, so answer from the Act.

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
Under the certified Companies (Amendment) Act, No. 12 of 2025, a struck-off company may apply to court within ten years of the Act's operation, join the Attorney-General, and show cause why it could not comply; the court may permit re-registration and order the return of property vested in the State [Act 12/2025 §17].

- The provision amends s.487(5) of the principal enactment, whose text is not in evidence [Act 12/2025 §17].
- Where the State has dealt with or disposed of the property, third-party rights acquired in good faith are unaffected; where it was destroyed, damaged, or never taken into possession, "the State shall not be liable to any party in any manner" [Act 12/2025 §17].

Caveats: The ten-year period runs from the Act's date of operation, and this is an amending Act, so the amended section's full current wording is not shown. A Gazette-text predecessor (582/2025 §17) became this Act; rely on the Act.

question: Under the revised Anti‑Corruption Act, in what situations will a person charged with a corruption offence be refused bail?
answer:
The evidence does not show the bail-refusal rule as law. The closest text is a clause that was **proposed but not enacted in those words** in the Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Bill (later Act 25/2026).

- As proposed, all offences would be "cognizable and non-bailable", with no bail except "in exceptional circumstances by a High Court" where the bribe was "not less than one hundred thousand rupees", or the loss or benefit "not less than five hundred thousand rupees", confirmed by a Director-General's certificate [063/2026 §17]; same text in the Gazette version [051/2026 §17].
- The earlier Anti-Corruption Gazette text would have required remand "until the conclusion of the trial", with bail only in "exceptional circumstances" for recorded reasons — but it is only a proposal and its later enactment is unchecked [311/2023 §149].
- Act 25/2026 makes no bail change visible here; its §17 concerns another provision [Act 25/2026].

Caveats: the enacted bail wording is missing from the evidence, so I cannot state the current refusal grounds.

question: Under the proposed Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters law, how are offences listed in Part B of the extradition schedule treated when Sri Lanka considers extraditing a suspect to another UN member state?
answer:
Under the proposed bill (Gazette text, not shown to have passed), offences in Part B of the Schedule to the Extradition Law are deemed **not** to be offences of a political character, or connected with/inspired by political motives, for extradition purposes between Sri Lanka and any UN Member State [073/2026 §11].

- The deeming applies "notwithstanding anything in the Extradition Law, No. 8 of 1977" and covers persons accused or convicted, and assistance under section 12 [073/2026 §11].
- Separately, an item for "an offence within the meaning of the Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters Act" is to be inserted immediately before Part B in that Schedule [073/2026 §8].

Caveats: this is a Gazette-text proposal, not an Act; identical text appears in 085/2026.

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
Under the National Environmental (Amendment) Act, No. 15 of 2026 (certified 2026-07-21), the substituted penalty in section 23r(2) is "a fine not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than one million rupees", plus "a fine of five thousand rupees for each day" the offence continues after conviction [Act 15/2026 §18].

- This replaces the earlier wording ("not less than rupees ten thousand and not exceeding rupees one hundred thousand", and "rupees five hundred for every day") [Act 15/2026 §18].
- The fine is imposed "on conviction before the Magistrate having jurisdiction" [Act 15/2026 §18].

Caveats: This is an amending Act, so it states the change to section 23r(2) of the National Environmental Act, No. 47 of 1980 rather than reproducing that Act's full current text.

question: What penalty does the amendment to the National Audit Act impose for the offence covered by Section 42?
answer:
The National Audit (Amendment) Act, No. 19 of 2025 (certified 2025-09-22) replaces Section 42's penalty with a fine "not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees" or imprisonment "not exceeding one year", or both [Act 19/2025 §13].

- This is an amending Act, not the consolidated principal Act, so it states the substitution only [Act 19/2025 §13].
- By contrast, the parallel Section 43(1) amendment allows up to three years' imprisonment [Act 19/2025 §14].

Caveats: The section's offence wording itself is not in the evidence; only the substituted penalty is shown.

question: Under the proposed Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs law, what fine and additional action apply if a dog owner does not vaccinate and register the dog after being given a notice?
answer:
A Rs 2,000 penalty plus the section 5 registration fee; the local authority must then vaccinate and register the dog itself "immediately" in the Register of Dogs [076/2026 §7(4)].

- The notice gives 14 days, extendable by a further 14 for reasonable cause accepted by the authorised officer [076/2026 §7(2)–(3)].
- The fee is "payable under section 5 to the local authority" [076/2026 §7(4)]; §5 requires registration on payment of a prescribed fee [066/2026 §5(1)].
- I rely on Bill 076/2026 (Bill, 2026-09-24); the identical clause appears in the Gazette text, 066/2026 (2026-09-07) [066/2026 §7(4)].

Caveats: This is a bill, not law — no certified Act is held, so it has not been shown to have passed.

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:
The amendment as passed—Act 27/2026 (certified 30 Oct 2026), formerly bill 062/2026—adds methamphetamine to the named drugs and creates a new manufacturing offence and penalty for other listed dangerous drugs [Act 27/2026 §2].

- Section 54A(1)(a) substitutes “heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium or methamphetamine” for “heroin or cocaine or morphine or opium” [Act 27/2026 §2].
- New paragraph (aa): manufacturing Groups A–E, Part I, Third Schedule drugs other than those five is an offence; on conviction by the High Court without a jury, the penalty is a fine “not less than two hundred thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees”, or imprisonment “not less than ten years and not exceeding twenty years”, or both [Act 27/2026 §2].
- The Third Schedule is also amended on cannabis entries [Act 27/2026 §5].

Caveat: this is an amending Act; the evidence does not give the consolidated Ordinance text.

question: Under the proposed Presidents' Entitlements repeal, will former presidents or their widows keep receiving housing, regular payments, secretarial assistance, official transport or a widow's pension once the new law takes effect?
answer:
No. This is now law, not a proposal: the Presidents' Entitlements (Repeal) Act, No. 18 of 2025 (certified 2025-09-10) repealed the 1986 Act [Act 18/2025 §2], and from commencement the listed benefits "shall no longer be provided with or paid to" [Act 18/2025 §3].

- Residence and monthly allowance to a former President or a former President's widow: stopped [Act 18/2025 §3(a)].
- Monthly secretarial allowance, official transport and other facilities: stopped [Act 18/2025 §3(b)].
- Widow's monthly pension: stopped [Act 18/2025 §3(c)].

Caveats: §3 covers benefits received "preceding the date of commencement"; the evidence does not give the commencement date, and only the repeal Act is in evidence — not the 1986 Act's own text.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Penal Code, what new penalty is introduced for intentionally causing serious injury to a child under 18?
answer:
The proposed amendment (bill 630/2025, the presented version of the Gazette text 618/2025) would punish voluntarily causing grievous hurt — serious injury — to a person under 18 with imprisonment "which may extend to ten years", plus a fine and possible compensation [618/2025 §6].

- It is a new section 316a of the Penal Code, except in the case provided for by section 326 [618/2025 §6].
- The court "may also be ordered to pay compensation", of an amount it determines after considering a victim impact statement from the National Authority for the Protection of Victims of Crime and Witnesses [618/2025 §6].

Caveats: this is a bill only (Gazette text 2025-07-08; presented version 2025-08-19) and has not been shown to have passed; the clause says "grievous hurt", not "serious injury", and the passage's heading refers to section 314a.

question: How does the proposed amendment to the Social Security Contribution Levy Act change the turnover limits and the applicable dates in Section 5, and what new limit is introduced for periods starting on 1 April 2026?
answer:
The Act as passed (Act 10/2026) amends Section 5 using **1 July 2026**, not 1 April 2026 — the earlier date appears only in the pre-presentation Gazette text, which the Act replaced.

- Act 10/2026 §3 amends s.5(1): in para (c) it substitutes "on or after January 1, 2024 and prior to July 1, 2026" and "sixty million rupees; or", and deletes the "or" in para (b) [Act 10/2026 §3].
- It adds a new para (d): "for any period commencing on or after July 1, 2026," turnover for "consecutive four quarters does not exceed thirty-six million rupees" [Act 10/2026 §3].
- The bill text (Gazette 017/2026 §3) used "April 1, 2026" for both changes; that wording was proposed but not enacted [017/2026 §3].

Caveats: No evidence shows s.5(1)(a)–(c) as they now read, so other existing turnover figures are unconfirmed.

question: What changes does the amendment to Section 14 of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act make to the ownership percentage requirement and to the type of entities mentioned in its subsections?
answer:
The amendment to Section 14 of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act, No. 36 of 2024 raises the ownership threshold from "more than fifty per centum" to "one hundred per centum" and replaces references to a "person" with a "company" (in subsection (2), one incorporated under the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007) [Act 14/2025 §12].

- Subsection (1): "more than fifty per centum" substituted by "one hundred per centum" [Act 14/2025 §12].
- Subsection (2): "Any person who" substituted by "Any company incorporated in terms of the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007, which" [Act 14/2025 §12].
- Subsection (3): "a person who" substituted by "a company, which" [Act 14/2025 §12].

Caveats: This is a certified amending Act (2025-08-18); it states the changes, not the amended Act's current text. The passage notes further parts of the section were not shown, and the other passage cited here concerns Section 18, not Section 14 [Act 14/2025 §14].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Trusts Ordinance, which part of Section 3 is being removed and how is the definition of “express trust” being changed?
answer:
The amendment would repeal **paragraph (n)** of Section 3 and narrow the "express trust" definition in paragraph (p) by dropping the word "generally": [081/2026 §2]

- Repeal: paragraph (n) of section 3 of the Trusts Ordinance (Chapter 87), as last amended by Act No. 6 of 2018, is "repealed": [081/2026 §2(1)] — the quoted words are from the passage but the sub-numbering shown is (1)/(2) within the section text.
- Definition: in paragraph (p), "for the words 'trust generally in the form', of the words 'trust in the form'": [081/2026 §2(2)]

Caveats: This is Gazette text dated 2026-10-14; it is a proposal and has not been shown to have passed (no certified Act held). The evidence does not set out the current text of paragraph (n) or the full definition, and part of section 3 is not shown.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
This is now law, not a proposal: Act 23/2026 (certified 2026-09-25), which came from bills 058/2026 and 064/2026, amends section 6 of the Judicature Act, No. 2 of 1978 [Act 23/2026 §3].

- The retirement age in section 6(3) is changed from "sixty-one years" to "sixty-three years" [Act 23/2026 §3(1)].
- Section 6(4) is repealed and replaced: "the age of retirement of all other Judges and Magistrates shall be sixty-two years", notwithstanding the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance (Chapter 355) [Act 23/2026 §3(2)].

Caveats: the Act only states the changes; the consolidated Judicature Act text is not in the evidence, and the Ordinance is not reproduced.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Universities Act, how many terms is a person allowed to serve as dean of a faculty?
answer:
Two terms — the amendment inserts a new subsection (4) providing that "No person shall be elected as the Dean of a Faculty for more than two terms" [Act 2/2026 §2].

- This is the Universities (Amendment) Act, No. 2 of 2026 (certified 2026-02-03), an amending Act that changes section 49 of the Universities Act No. 16 of 1978; it is law, not a bill [Act 2/2026 §2].
- The earlier Gazette text (bill 649/2025) had the same two-term limit but worded it "appointed as the Dean" rather than "elected"; the Act's wording governs [649/2025 §2].

Caveats: The amended section 49 as it now reads in full is not in the evidence.

question: What 2025 legislation establishes the professional facilities‑management institute as a legal corporate body in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The bill is **623/2025, Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka (Incorporation)** (Gazette text, 2025-07-18); an identical text also appears in 628/2025. However, it is a **proposal, not law** — no certified Act for it is held (Acts checked to 2026-10-30), so it has not been shown to have passed.

- Clause 2(1) would give the Institute "perpetual succession" under the name "Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka", with power to sue and be sued and to use a common seal [623/2025 §2].
- Clause 2(2) would make the body corporate represent members' majority interests and "uphold the professional standards of the Facilities Management profession" [623/2025 §2].

Caveats: I have not verified whether a corresponding Act exists; the evidence contains no certified version.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 623/2025 §2

question: Which 2025 legislation creates a legal corporation for the charitable foundation named after senior monk Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero?
answer:
No enacted 2025 law is shown: the incorporation is only in bills — Bill 596/2025 (presented 2025-05-08) and its earlier Gazette text 581/2025 (2025-04-10). No certified Act is held, so it has not been shown to have passed.

- Both provide that members "shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession" under the name "Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation" [596/2025 §2; 581/2025 §2].
- The short title proposed is the "... Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation) Act, No. of 2025" [596/2025 §1].

Caveats: The title matches, but these are proposals, not law; the Bill version (596/2025) is the later text.

question: What 2026 amendment revises the Act that governs marriage and divorce among the Kandyan community (Chapter 113)?
answer:
The 2026 amendment is the **Kandyan Marriage and Divorce (Amendment)** bill — Gazette text **008/2026 (2026-02-05)**, with identical clause text in **016/2026 (Bill, 2026-02-19)**. It is a proposal only; no certified Act is held for it, so it has not been shown to have passed [008/2026 §2] [016/2026].

- It amends section 32 of the principal enactment (Chapter 113) by substituting paragraph (a) with “Adultery by the husband or wife after marrige.” [008/2026 §2] (the spelling “marrige” appears in the Gazette text; 016/2026's summary renders it “marriage”).
- It also repeals paragraph (b) of section 32 [008/2026 §2].

Caveats: Only section 32 and the citation clause appear in the evidence; the rest of the bill's text is not shown.

question: What is the 2026 legislation that establishes the Al‑Hashimi Association as a legal corporate entity?
answer:
The 2026 proposal is the **Al‑Hashimi Association (Incorporation)** bill — the newest version we hold is Bill 039/2026 (Bill, 2026‑05‑21), with identical text in Bill 024/2026 (Gazette text, 2026‑04‑08). Neither is law: no certified Act for it is held (Acts checked to 2026‑10‑30), so it has not been shown to have passed.

- §2(1) would give members "perpetual succession under the name and style of the 'Al‑Hashimi Association'", with power to sue and be sued and a common seal [024/2026 §2].
- §2(2) would deem the body corporate a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [024/2026 §2].
- §3 sets the objects (poverty relief, poor students, youth self‑employment, fund‑raising, asset trust), non‑discriminatorily [024/2026 §3].

Caveats: This is a bill, not an Act; its commencement wording ("from and after the date of commencement of this Act") is proposed only.

question: Which 2026 bill repeals the 2009 act that created the position of chief of the defence staff in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) bill — it became **Act No. 22 of 2026** (certified 2026-09-22), and repeals the Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009 [Act 22/2026 §2].

- It originated as bill 036/2026 (Gazette text, 2026-05-15) and 059/2026 (Bill, 2026-08-04) [Act 22/2026 §2].
- Section 2 states simply: "The Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009 is hereby repealed" [Act 22/2026 §2].
- Holders of the office of Chief of Defence Staff and Committee members cease to hold office from commencement [Act 22/2026 §3(1)].

Caveats: The bill is now law, so the Act governs; the evidence does not include the text of the 2009 Act itself.

question: What 2025 legislation modifies the 1988 Provincial Councils Elections Act in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2025 proposal is the **Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment)** bill — Gazette text 589/2025 (2025-05-22), with identical text in 605/2025 (Bill, 2025-06-05). It is a proposal only: no certified Act is held for it, so it has not been shown to have passed.

- §2 restores the 1988 Act "in force on September 21, 2017" notwithstanding the amendments by Act No. 17 of 2017, operative "with effect from the date of coming into force of this Act" [589/2025 §2].
- Acts done from 22 September 2017 to commencement are preserved "insofar as such act is not inconsistent with" the 1988 Act [589/2025 §2].
- Short title: "Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment) Act, No. of 2025" [589/2025 §1].

Caveats: Neither 589/2025 nor 605/2025 is law in the evidence; an equivalent 2023 proposal exists [322/2023 §3].

question: Which 2025 bill amends the 2016 Act that provides a financial assistance scheme for workers?
answer:
The 2016 Act is the **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 4 of 2016**, amended by the **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment) Act, No. 10 of 2025** (certified 2025-07-23), which came from Gazette bill **587/2025** (2025-05-20) and bill **602/2025** (2025-06-03) [Act 10/2025 §2]; [587/2025]; [602/2025].

- Section 3(1) and (2) of the 2016 Act are amended so the periods ending "March 31, 2025" replace open-ended starts [Act 10/2025 §2].
- The Act is deemed to have come into operation on April 1, 2025 [Act 10/2025 §1].
- A separate Act 9/2025 amends the different 2005 Act, No. 36 of 2005 — not the 2016 Act [Act 9/2025].

Caveats: this is an amending Act, so the amended 2016 text itself is not in evidence.

question: Which 2025 bill seeks to amend the 2016 legislation that establishes the minimum wage for employees in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 604/2025 (National Minimum Wage of Workers (Amendment)), presented 2025-06-03, sought to amend the National Minimum Wage of Workers Act, No. 3 of 2016; the same text appears in Gazette bill 586/2025 of 2025-05-20 [604/2025 §2] [586/2025].

- Both bills became Act No. 11 of 2025 (certified 2025-07-23), which is the law; the Act's wording differs from the bills, so rely on it [Act 11/2025 §2].
- The amendment substitutes the wage floor: Rs 27,000 monthly/Rs 1,080 daily from 1 April 2025 to 31 December 2025, then Rs 30,000/Rs 1,200 from 1 January 2026 [Act 11/2025 §2].
- It also merges budgetary relief allowances into the minimum wage and bars wage cuts that negate the increase [Act 11/2025 §3] [Act 11/2025 §4].

Caveats: The evidence does not include the full text of the 2016 Act.

question: Which 2025 amendment alters the 2005 law that established the workers' special financial assistance allowance?
answer:
The **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment) Act, No. 9 of 2025** (certified 2025-07-23) — no bill in the evidence uses the name "special financial assistance allowance", so this is the closest-titled match; it amends the Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 36 of 2005 [Act 9/2025 §2].

- It substitutes in section 3(1) of the 2005 Act "For the period commencing on August 1, 2005 and ending on March 31, 2025, " for "With effect from August 1, 2005" [Act 9/2025 §2].
- It came from bills 588/2025 (Gazette text, 2025-05-20) and 603/2025 (Bill, 2025-06-03), which are superseded by the Act [Act 9/2025 §2].
- Its provisions are deemed to have come into operation on April 1, 2025 [Act 9/2025 §1].

Caveats: The evidence does not show the full text of the 2005 Act or use the phrase "special financial assistance allowance", so I cannot confirm that is the scheme amended.

question: What 2026 legislation proposes to abolish the 1977 law that provided retirement benefits to Sri Lankan parliamentarians?
answer:
The **Parliamentary Pensions (Repeal) Act, No. 5 of 2026** (certified 2026-02-17) — its long title is "to repeal the Parliamentary Pensions Law, No. 1 of 1977" — repeals that 1977 law [Act 5/2026 §4].

- It began as bill 001/2026 (published 2026-01-07); the Act's wording differs from the bill, so the Act governs [Act 5/2026 §4][001/2026 §4].
- From commencement, people receiving a pension under the 1977 Law, or under section 9 of Act No. 1 of 1982 or section 9 of Act No. 47 of 1990, "cease to receive that pension" [Act 5/2026].
- The text states no new powers, obligations or penalties [Act 5/2026].

Caveats: The summaries are auto-generated hints; the clause text is the authority, and if Sinhala and Tamil texts conflict the Sinhala prevails [Act 5/2026 §4].

question: Which 2025 bill sought to modify the 1988 Sri Lankan law that imposes a tax on gambling activities?
answer:
Two 2025 bills sought to amend the Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No. 40 of 1988: the Gazette text 640/2025 (2025-10-02) and the presented bill 642/2025 (2025-10-21), both now Act No. 25 of 2025 (certified 2025-12-17) [640/2025] [642/2025] [Act 25/2025 §2].

- Both bills proposed an 18% rate from 1 October 2025; the certified Act instead sets 18% for years "commencing on or after January 1, 2026" [642/2025] [Act 25/2025 §2(1)(c)].
- The Act also raises the amount in subsection (1AA) from "United States Dollars fifty" to "one hundred" [Act 25/2025 §2(2)].

Caveats: These are amending instruments; the amended 1988 Act's consolidated text is not in the evidence.

question: Which 2025 bill proposes changes to the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464)?
answer:
Both 2025 Land Development (Amendment) bills amend the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464), with identical clause text: 617/2025 [Gazette text, 2025-07-04] and 625/2025 [Bill, 2025-07-22], the later presented version [625/2025 §1][617/2025 §1].

- Repeals "or upon his or her marriage" in s.48A 2(c) [625/2025 §2].
- Repeals s.48B 1(a) [625/2025 §3].
- In s.68(1), substitutes "fails without reasonable cause to succeed" for "fails to succeed" [625/2025 §4].

Caveats: Neither has been shown to have passed; no certified Act is held [625/2025]. An earlier 2024 bill (519/2024) has similar text [519/2024].

question: Which 2026 bill updates the 2018 Finance Act No. 35?
answer:
The **Finance (Amendment) bill, No. 034/2026 (Bill, 2026-05-06)** — its text is identical to the earlier Gazette text 027/2026 (2026-04-23) — which amends section 44 of the Finance Act, No. 35 of 2018 on the cellular-tower levy [034/2026 §2].

- It would exempt newly constructed towers commencing commercial operations on or after 1 January 2026, "for a period of five years" [034/2026 §2].
- It is a proposal only; no certified Act for it is held, so it has not been shown to have passed [034/2026 §2].

Caveats: Act 11/2026 (Inland Revenue (Amendment), certified 2026-06-03) only lists the 2018 Finance Act in an interest write-off provision, and amends the Inland Revenue Act, not the Finance Act [Act 11/2026 §42].

question: Which 2026 bill revises the 1956 law that sets rules for female workers, teenage employees and child labor?
answer:
The Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) bill — Gazette text 044/2026 (2026-06-25), presented as bill 056/2026 (2026-07-22) — to amend Act No. 47 of 1956. It is now law as Act 21/2026 (certified 2026-09-08), so the Act is the reliable text [Act 21/2026 §1].

- The Act substitutes "one hundred thousand rupees" for "ten thousand rupees" in sections 7(3), 13(2) and 20A(3) of the 1956 Act [Act 21/2026 §2][Act 21/2026 §3].
- The higher amounts do not apply to offences committed before the Act came into operation [Act 21/2026 §5].
- Sinhala text prevails over Tamil on inconsistency [Act 21/2026 §6].

Caveats: The evidence covers only these fine amendments, not the rest of the 1956 Act's rules on women, young persons and children.

question: Which 2025 bill proposes to revoke the 2024 legislation that introduced internet safety and content regulation measures?
answer:
The Online Safety (Repeal) Bill — Gazette text 578/2025 (2025-04-08), presented as Bill 590/2025 (2025-05-08) — which states: "The Online Safety Act, No. 9 of 2024 is hereby repealed" [578/2025 §2].

- It also repeals "Any regulations made under the Online Safety Act, No. 9 of 2024, after its enactment" [590/2025 §3].
- Short title: "Online Safety (Repeal) Act, No. of 2025" [590/2025 §1].

question: What 2025 legislation addresses re‑conducting postponed local council elections by allowing new nominations and setting a fresh election date?
answer:
The **Local Authorities Elections (Special Provisions) Act, No. 1 of 2025** (certified 2025-02-17) — it came from bills 565/2025 (Gazette text, 2025-01-01) and 566/2025 (Bill, 2025-01-09) [Act 1/2025].

- It deems earlier nomination papers for the listed local authorities "of no force and effect as if such nomination papers had never been submitted", and revokes the earlier notices [Act 1/2025 §2].
- The fresh nomination date is fixed by the Election Commission "by Order published in the Gazette", "not later than three months from the date of coming into operation of this Act" [Act 1/2025 §3].
- Deposits are refunded on production of the receipt [Act 1/2025 §2].

Caveats: the Act itself sets no polling date; polls proceed under the Local Authorities Elections Ordinance at a date the Commission determines.

question: Which 2025 bill updates the 2008 act that governs major strategic development projects in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2025 bill was the Strategic Development Projects (Amendment) Bill — 643/2025 (Gazette text, 2025-11-07), presented as 650/2025 (Bill, 2025-11-14) — which became Act No. 26 of 2025 (certified 2025-12-17) [643/2025][650/2025][Act 26/2025 §2].

- It amends the Strategic Development Projects Act, No. 14 of 2008, as last amended by Act No. 12 of 2011 [Act 26/2025 §2].
- Main change: “twenty-five years” in the section 2 proviso is replaced with “ten years” [Act 26/2025 §2].
- It also substitutes new sections 3 and 4 (identification, Finance Ministry ex-ante cost-benefit analysis within one month, monitoring, penalties) [Act 26/2025 §3][Act 26/2025 §4].

Caveats: 643/2025 and 650/2025 are proposals only; the law is Act 26/2025, and the amending Act does not set out the 2008 Act's full amended text.

question: Which 2026 bill was introduced to legally establish the UnV charitable foundation?
answer:
Bill 010/2026, the **UnV Foundation (Incorporation)** bill (2026-01-22), presented by Hon. Imran Maharoof, M.P. [010/2026]. An identical earlier Gazette text exists as Bill 003/2026 (2026-01-09) [003/2026].

- Clause 2 would make the Foundation a body corporate with perpetual succession, suing/sealing powers, and deem it a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [003/2026 §2].

Caveats: It is a bill only — no certified Act is held for it (Acts checked to 2026-10-30), so it has not been shown to have passed.

question: Which 2025 bill updates Sri Lanka's 1979 criminal procedure legislation?
answer:
Bill 576/2025 — Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment), Gazette text dated 2025-03-28 — is the 2025 bill amending the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979; it became Act No. 7 of 2025 (certified 2025-06-20), and the Act states it came from bills 576/2025 and 579/2025 [576/2025] [Act 7/2025].

- The Act's long title is "TO AMEND THE CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE ACT, NO. 15 OF 1979" [Act 7/2025].
- It inserts new sections 144A and 144B, letting a Magistrate "dispense with the personal attendance in court of a suspect or an accused" for detention extension, bail, investigation assistance or "any other purpose" [Act 7/2025 §2].
- The Gazette text adds the same sections; being a bill, it was only a proposal [576/2025].

Caveats: The Act is an amending Act, so it states changes, not the 1979 Code's current text. A separate 2024 bill (550/2024) is not shown to have passed.

question: What 2026 bill proposes the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution?
answer:
Bill 065/2026, the **Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution** (Bill, 2026-08-18; Gazette text 057/2026, 2026-08-07), is the 2026 bill carrying that title [065/2026 §1][057/2026 §1]. It is a bill only — no certified Act is held for it, so it has not been shown to have passed [065/2026 §1].

- It replaces Article 107(5): Supreme Court judges retire at 67, Court of Appeal judges at 65, and the Chief Justice retires at 67 or six years after appointment, whichever is earlier [065/2026 §2].
- It amends Article 137 to allow "not more than twenty four other Judges" instead of nineteen [065/2026 §3].
- An identically titled Twenty Second Amendment bill exists from 2022 [246/2022], which is a different bill.

Caveats: the auto-generated summary of 065/2026 misstates the retirement age as "67 to 67 (no change)"; the clause text above governs.

Caveats: the question's "Tenancy Act" name does not match the evidence; the auto-generated summaries describe it as an "Act", which the passage status contradicts.

question: What 2026 legislation creates a corporate entity for the Mahawilachchiya children’s education centre?
answer:
